decks.name: LeetCode #98 - Validate Binary Search Tree
decks.description: Determine if a binary tree is a valid binary search tree

cards.question: Validate Binary Search Tree: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST). A valid BST is defined as follows: The left subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys less than the node's key. The right subtree of a node contains only nodes with keys greater than the node's key. Both the left and right subtrees must also be binary search trees.

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.explanation: For each node, use helper function to verify all nodes in left subtree are less than current value and all nodes in right subtree are greater. Recursively validate left and right subtrees are also BSTs. Redundant validations as nodes are checked multiple times leading to O(n²) time complexity. Simple but inefficient approach.

solutions.name: Depth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use recursive DFS with min and max bounds for valid node values. Each node must be within (min, max) range. For left child, update max bound to current value. For right child, update min bound to current value. Start with (-infinity, +infinity) bounds. Single pass through tree with O(n) time. Clean and efficient solution.

solutions.name: Breadth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use BFS with queue storing (node, min, max) tuples. For each node, check if value is within bounds. Add left child with (min, node.val) bounds and right child with (node.val, max) bounds to queue. Process until queue empty or invalid node found. Iterative approach avoiding recursion with O(n) time and space.
